audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were wrong or absent. (a) The page tells you to 'eat the suppress' and Feast him afterwards. Infinite Duress is flagged as a channel - 'interruptible: any CC cancels it' - so Rupture's knockup breaks it outright as he lands. (b) Primal Howl is never mentioned anywhere, despite being 2.5 seconds of damage reduction that ends in a fear on an 11-to-15-second cooldown.
audit.why: Interrupting a 110-second ultimate is worth more than surviving it, and walking into an unmentioned fear undoes any Cho'Gath commit.
audit.corrected: Rupture him as Infinite Duress lands to cancel the channel; Feral Scream denies Jaws of the Beast; respect Primal Howl's damage reduction and its fear.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late-game text says Warwick 'has no max-HP or true damage to cut through your stacks' and that stacking Feast makes you safe from him. Jaws of the Beast deals damage based on the target's maximum health.
audit.why: Riot's description: 'bites his target, dealing damage based on their maximum health and healing for damage dealt', and the kit carries the percentHealth flag. Feast stacks therefore increase what his Q hits you for, so Grievous Wounds and resistances do the work that raw HP cannot.
audit.corrected: Removed the claim; anti-heal is the answer, and HP alone is not.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven stages were given to Warwick and the lane rated EVEN 6/10, against a 54.95% Cho'Gath win rate over 182 games and prose that says 'this is where the lane flips to you' at 4-5.
audit.why: The chart contradicts both the win rate and the page's own mid-game text.
audit.corrected: FAV, 6.5/10; chart Skill / Warwick / Warwick / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath with ratings 5,4,4,6,7,7,7.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes had no cooldown anchors and treated Blood Hunt as a permanent state.
audit.why: Blood Hunt is his W on 80/70/60/50/40s, Jaws of the Beast is 8 down to 6s, Primal Howl 15 down to 11s, Infinite Duress 110/90/70s. Eternal Hunger's healing steps at 50% and triples at 25% health, which is what actually defines the danger window.
audit.corrected: Levels 2-3 are his; 4-5 onward yours; 6 is yours because Rupture cancels a 110-second ultimate and Feast is true damage.

edits.before: Levels 2-3 are the danger window. Warwick's Q heals him on every hit in a sustained trade, and once you dip below half HP his Blood Hunt move speed lets him close and stick to you before your Carnivore sustain ramps. Don't burn Rupture chasing him with E autos — if you whiff your knock-up you have no follow-up and his drain wins the exchange. Hold Q until he commits, last-hit safely with Carnivore topping you off, and accept a little chip knowing your sustain catches up fast.
edits.after: Levels 2-3 are the danger window. Jaws of the Beast bites for a share of your maximum health and heals him for the damage it deals, on a cooldown that starts at 8 seconds, and once you dip below half HP his Blood Hunt gives him move speed straight at you. Don't burn Rupture chasing him with E autos - if you whiff the knockup you have no follow-up and his drain wins the exchange. Hold Q until he commits, last-hit safely with Carnivore topping you off, and buy your Grievous Wounds component early rather than late.

edits.before: This is where the lane flips to you. Land Rupture to knock him up, immediately Feral Scream to silence his Q so he can't heal through the trade, then chunk him with Vorpal Spikes while Carnivore keeps you topped. At 6, Feast answers his whole kit: point-blank true damage that ignores his bonus HP and lifesteal, so when he ults onto you and suppresses, you Feast him out of it as the lock ends. Bait the all-in, eat the suppress, and execute him through the dive.
edits.after: This is where the lane flips to you. Land Rupture to knock him up, immediately Feral Scream to silence Jaws of the Beast so he cannot heal through the trade, then chunk him with Vorpal Spikes while Carnivore keeps you topped. At 6 the answer is not to survive his ultimate but to cancel it: Infinite Duress is an interruptible channel, so a Rupture dropped where he lands ends a 110-second cooldown before the suppress finishes. Then Feast through his bonus HP.

edits.before: You take over completely. Stacked Feast and tank items make you a bulky HP monster, and unlike Fiora or a percent-HP shredder, Warwick has no max-HP or true damage to cut through your stacks — his heal-more-vs-low-HP passive simply can't out-pace your bulk. His R suppress is still a real engage onto your backline, so save Rupture or Feral Scream to interrupt his ult dive, then peel and Feast him off your carries. Owned in the 1v1, and a wall to body-block his ult in every teamfight.
edits.after: You take over the fight, but not the way the old advice said. Feast stacks make you enormous, and Jaws of the Beast deals damage based on your maximum health - so every stack you add is more damage taken from that bite, and Grievous Wounds plus resistances do the work raw HP cannot. What you do own is the interruption: his R is a channel, so Rupture or Feral Scream cancels the ult dive onto your backline, and Primal Howl's fear is on 11 seconds at rank 5, so bait it before you commit. Peel, cancel, Feast.

notes: The claim that Warwick has no max-health damage was the most dangerous thing on this page - it told a Cho'Gath player that Feast stacking makes him safe, when Jaws of the Beast scales with the exact stat he is stacking. Also note chogath.json tags Rupture (Q) with grounding, which is a tooltip-parse misfire on 'Ruptures the ground' (same false positive on Malphite Q and Olaf Q); I wrote only the knockup. Warwick's R is flagged interruptible by the kit, but whether the suppression itself is cleansable or reduced by tenacity is not in the data, so I did not say.
